newsitem.title: IRAN: U.N. expands schooling for Afghan girls in Iran.
newsitem.headline: U.N. expands schooling for Afghan girls in Iran.

text.p: The United Nations is providing an incentive to get Afghan and Iraqi schoolgirls into classrooms at refugee camps in Iran -- a can of cooking oil for a month of attendance.
The "Oil for Schooling of Girls" scheme was launched on March 11 by the World Food Programme, the U.N. information centre in Tehran said in a statement on Thursday.

"This scheme provides Afghan and Iraqi refugee girls with a 4.6 kg can of (cooking) oil for every month of attendance at school," it said. "The aim of this programme is to encourage parents of refugee girls to enrol their daughters in schools and to continue to send them on a regular basis."
The scheme will be implemented in six Afghan camps and 26 Iraqi camps benefiting 5,800 Iraqi girls and 1,200 Afghan girls.
Iran hosts two million refugees from Afghanistan and Iraq.
In Afghanistan itself, in areas controlled by the purist Islamic Taleban, female students have been banned from educational establishments.
